_notes: Single source for tooltips, the glossary on /learn and the learning API. Terms used by the tutorials and missions.

terms.short: A virtual entitlement to performance payouts. It is not ownership of the player, their salary or their team.
The game currency. Every account starts with $100,000; it cannot be cashed out.
The best price someone will pay right now. You sell at the bid.
The best price someone will sell for right now. You buy at the ask.
The gap between bid and ask. A small toll you pay every time you trade.
A model estimate of discounted future performance payments. It can be wrong and is not an executable price.
Buy or sell right now at the best available price. Fast, no haggling.
A small cut (0.10%) taken on every trade. Lots of tiny trades add up.
Profit you've locked in by selling. Money in the bank.
Profit on shares you still hold. It can still vanish if the price drops.
A run of big games. Prices often jump - and the hype often fades a bit afterwards.
How jumpy a price is. High volatility = stormy weather on the ticker.
Virtual dollars available for purchases or reserved by open buy orders. Payouts increase this balance.
Cash plus holdings at current quote midpoints plus pending payout estimates. The competition uses net liquidation value instead.
A dealer quoting buy and sell prices with finite cash and shares. A quote can disappear when inventory or cash runs out.
The extra you pay when a big order eats through the best price and fills at worse ones.
An order with your price on it. It waits until the market comes to you, and never pays more than your limit.
A safety net: it sells your shares automatically if the bid falls to the price you set.
How far the quoted price sits above the analyst estimate. The estimate can be wrong; the gap need not close.
One bar on the chart: where the price opened, closed, and how high and low it went in that time.
Spreading money across players and teams reduces exposure to any one outcome; it does not guarantee a profit.
Cash plus estimated proceeds from selling all holdings after fees and price impact, plus pending payment rights. Paid dividends are already in cash.
$0.02 per positive Game Score point per share. Hold at the synthetic noon cutoff; actual game performance settles at day close. A missed game pays zero.
